tasks.short: Assess project risks and agree response strategies.

steps.what: Collect project changes, incidents, supplier concerns and technical assessment findings.
Explore failure scenarios with business, technical and security specialists.
Write distinct risk statements with causes, consequences and supporting evidence.

loop.input: Workshop notes, technical findings and existing risk entries.
loop.output: Source-linked risk statements with possible duplicates and missing information flagged.
loop.check: Require evidence references and cause-event-impact fields; project manager checks meaning and duplicate decisions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unsupported entries remain excluded pending review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe the same risks differently and need semantic interpretation.

steps.what: Assess likelihood, impact, existing controls and uncertainty using the agreed risk scale.
Select responses, contingency triggers, action owners and target dates.
Approve response spending and accept or escalate residual risk within delegated authority.
Update the risk register and assign approved response actions.

tasks.design: An integration gathers approved evidence from the {PROJECT}, {HELPDESK}, {PROCUREMENT} and {DOCS}; a bounded loop proposes source-linked risk entries. Configure a risk register, scoring calculations, action reminders and escalation thresholds in the {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW}. Specialists assess uncertain impacts, and authorised people approve responses and residual-risk acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Risk evidence is fragmented and workshop notes need manual translation into register entries. Risk scores also depend on judgement that software cannot remove.
tasks.enabler_now: Adapters and register workflows are easier to build. Bounded extraction can reduce paperwork without giving a model authority to accept risk.
tasks.still_hard: Unknown failure modes, weak control evidence and correlated risks resist simple scoring. A tidy register can still create false confidence.
tasks.human_edge: Surface uncomfortable scenarios, challenge control claims and decide which uncertainty the business can bear.

ambition.what: Weekly reassessment of risks affected by scope changes

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time maintaining the register and more time testing response readiness. They can trigger agreed reviews and contingency checks; residual-risk acceptance stays with authorised owners.

reach.task: Test project contingency triggers against service recovery needs.
reach.learn: Business impact analysis, recovery objectives and scenario exercises.

evidence.claim: Configured registers and escalation rules can automate tracking while retaining human risk acceptance.
Existing security scanning can supply technical findings; those findings do not constitute a complete project risk assessment.
Documented automated metadata filling can be wrong, supporting explicit review of extracted risk entries.

assumptions: The scope covers project risk management, not a replacement for specialist security or legal assessment.
Existing technical assessments supply findings; this build does not create a scanning service.
Time shares and remaining percentages are estimates.
Evidence access and retention follow GDPR; EU AI Act applicability is assessed for the actual use.
Employee consultation is included where national rules apply; unresolved statutory timelines may extend rollout.
unknowns: Which risk criteria and acceptance authorities are formally approved.
Whether specialist findings and control evidence are accessible.
Which risk records contain sensitive employee, supplier or security information.
Which sector-specific obligations apply to the organisation.
research_questions: Which changes should trigger reassessment rather than another routine reminder?
Can extraction preserve uncertainty and distinguish existing incidents from future risks?
new_work: Review extracted risk statements and evidence links.
Resolve duplicate entries and unsupported control claims.
Maintain risk criteria, escalation thresholds and access permissions.
Check response actions and contingency readiness.
tasks.statement: Perform risk assessments to develop response strategies.

tasks.short: Check deliverable quality, secure release approval and submit the approved package.

steps.what: Collect the deliverable version, acceptance criteria and quality evidence.
Check required tests, documents, approvals and version consistency.
Compare narrative evidence with acceptance criteria and identify unexplained gaps.

loop.input: Version-pinned acceptance criteria and linked narrative quality evidence.
loop.output: A criterion-by-criterion evidence map with supported, missing and uncertain findings.
loop.check: Require criterion identifiers and evidence references; the quality lead verifies every proposed finding.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction pass per package; missing sources or ambiguity leave the criterion unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules check required files and test outcomes, but narrative evidence uses different wording from acceptance criteria.

steps.what: Judge fitness for use and recommend release, rework or an explicit waiver.
Approve submission of the specified version and any permitted quality waiver.
Submit the approved version to the agreed recipient.
Record submission evidence and link the receipt to the deliverable.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} assembles a version-pinned package from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, runs deterministic completeness checks and requests a bounded evidence-map draft for narrative criteria. The quality lead reviews fitness for use, the business owner approves submission, and the project manager confirms the recipient before the {EMAIL} sends the package and the {PROJECT} records delivery evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deliverables, test evidence and approvals refer to different versions. Narrative acceptance criteria resist simple completeness checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Version identifiers and configured approvals can bind checks to the exact package. A bounded model can draft an evidence map for review without deciding acceptance.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence can be incomplete or misleading, and passing tests does not prove fitness for use. Contractual acceptance and quality waivers require authorised judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the deliverable meets the real business need and recognise defects that a checklist misses.

ambition.what: Pre-submission readiness reviews for small internal IT projects

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling packages and chasing approval evidence to resolving material quality gaps. The project manager gains clearer authority to block submission when required evidence is missing; acceptance and waiver rights remain with authorised owners.

reach.task: Design acceptance controls and analyse recurring deliverable defects.
reach.learn: Evidence traceability, risk-based sampling and corrective-action verification.

evidence.claim: Version-bound completeness checks and approval workflows can automate package handling while preserving human release authority.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrates prompt-based document metadata extraction and warns of errors; it does not establish acceptance-review reliability.

assumptions: The scenario includes submission to an external recipient; internal-only projects can use an internal delivery action.
Mandatory quality controls cannot be waived unless policy and contract explicitly permit it.
A changed package invalidates earlier checks and approval; failed checks return rework actions to the delivery owner.
A submission receipt proves delivery, not business acceptance.
Build ranges cover package handling and evidence mapping, excluding development of new technical test suites.
Time estimates require pilot validation. GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and consultation under national rules must be assessed.
unknowns: Which quality checks are mandatory and which evidence is machine-readable.
Who may approve submission, accept deliverables and authorise waivers.
Whether recipients use the {EMAIL}, the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or another approved channel.
Whether contracts require signatures or a separate acceptance process.
Access, retention and consultation requirements for the evidence set.
research_questions: Which quality checks can run deterministically against versioned evidence?
How often does the draft evidence map miss material gaps or cite irrelevant evidence?
Can existing approval configuration invalidate approval automatically when the package changes?
new_work: Review evidence maps and correct unsupported coverage findings.
Maintain quality checklists, acceptance mappings and waiver permissions.
Handle failed submissions, recipient changes and missing receipts.
Investigate version mismatches and verify approval invalidation.
tasks.statement: Submit project deliverables, ensuring adherence to quality standards.

tasks.short: Review project team contributions, discuss feedback and document agreed support.

steps.what: Review agreed deliverables, progress, blockers and previous commitments.
Ask the team member about context, dependencies and support needs.
Form balanced feedback and decide which support or escalation is appropriate.
Discuss feedback, hear disagreement and agree practical next steps.
Write the feedback record and action dates in the restricted personnel record.
Send reminders about agreed actions and the next discussion.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted factual view in {PROJECT} showing agreed deliverables, blockers and commitments. A structured form in {TALENT}, or restricted {DOCS} where needed, captures human-written feedback and drives agreed reminders through {WORKFLOW}; it produces no individual scores or inferred assessments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery facts and private feedback notes lived in separate places. Automating assessment would also miss context and risk damaging trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record permissions, configurable forms and scheduled reminders handle much of the preparation and follow-up. Small integrations can connect approved facts without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Attributing outcomes fairly and discussing difficult feedback remain human work. GDPR applies; national rules may require employee consultation, and an employee-evaluation extension would require EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding circumstances, listening to disagreement and giving feedback that changes behaviour without undermining trust.

ambition.what: Fortnightly support-intervention review for blocked team members.

tasks.altitude: More time goes into coaching and removing blockers, with less preparation and reminder chasing. Formal appraisal and employment decision rights remain with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Investigate recurring process blockers across project teams.
reach.learn: Process mapping, contextual comparison and separating system constraints from individual contribution.

evidence.claim: Configured factual views, restricted records and reminders can reduce preparation without automating performance judgement.
Project activity measures alone do not establish an individual's performance or explain delivery problems.
The digest identifies Dutch works council consent provisions relevant to employee-monitoring systems.

assumptions: The project manager gives project feedback; the line manager retains formal appraisal responsibility.
The factual view uses declared project records rather than message analysis or passive activity tracking.
The employee can discuss and correct the factual basis of feedback.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Consent and access ranges include consultation preparation and access design; formal processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which feedback records may the project manager access and retain?
What national consultation requirements apply to the proposed factual view?
Does an existing {TALENT} form meet the team's needs?
Which delivery facts are reliable enough to show without misleading context?
research_questions: Does the factual view improve preparation without encouraging simplistic comparisons?
Which record fields help follow-through while minimising personal data?
new_work: Correct inaccurate delivery facts before feedback discussions.
Maintain access permissions and retention settings.
Check reminders against changed agreements.
Review whether the view is drifting into employee scoring.
tasks.statement: Monitor the performance of project team members, providing and documenting performance feedback.

tasks.short: Work with project personnel to understand problems and agree practical resolutions.

steps.what: Read issue records, delivery updates and relevant team messages.
Prepare an issue brief with evidence, open questions and affected dependencies.

loop.input: Authorised issue records and explicitly linked messages, plus the project baseline.
loop.output: An issue brief separating reported facts, disagreements and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require source references for factual statements; the project manager checks omissions and sensitive wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per issue; missing or conflicting evidence returns to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template can organise the brief, but relevant explanations and disagreements appear in free text.

steps.what: Discuss causes, constraints and disagreements with the people involved.
Agree a technical resolution and identify changes requiring escalation.
Record the agreed resolution, action owners and due dates.
Send follow-ups when agreed actions become overdue.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} supplies issue records and explicitly linked {CHAT} messages to a bounded drafting loop that prepares a source-linked brief in the {DOCS}. People discuss the problem and approve the resolution, while structured decisions feed configured action records and reminders in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The useful context sits across messages and issue records. The central conversation involves trust, disagreement and incomplete technical knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded model can prepare a brief from a limited evidence set. Existing action forms and reminders can handle the paperwork once people agree.
tasks.still_hard: People may conceal uncertainty, disagree about causes or lack capacity to deliver the proposed fix. Better preparation does not remove those constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Create enough trust for people to admit problems, challenge an attractive explanation and negotiate a workable commitment.

ambition.what: A recurring cross-team dependency resolution clinic

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into reconstructing issues and chasing routine actions. The project manager can convene cross-team resolution sessions; technical decisions and scope approvals retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Trace a recurring project blocker to an interface or requirements mismatch.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, requirements validation and evidence-based root-cause analysis.

evidence.claim: Configured action registers and reminders can automate follow-up while the resolution conversation remains human.
TOPdesk summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review, demonstrating related bounded text preparation.

assumptions: Only issue-linked, authorised messages enter the brief; private conversations are excluded.
Agreed decisions are captured in structured fields during the discussion.
The technical lead may approve technical resolutions within existing scope; change requests follow sponsor approval.
Time shares and build ranges are pilot estimates. GDPR access controls and national consultation requirements apply.
unknowns: Whether issue records contain links to the relevant evidence.
Which discussions may be processed and under what retention policy.
Who can approve technical resolutions and cross-team commitments.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed message processing.
research_questions: Does a source-linked brief reduce preparation time without suppressing disagreement?
Which issue types benefit from a brief, and which are quicker to discuss directly?
Can existing action forms capture commitments without creating duplicate records?
new_work: Check brief sources, omissions and disputed statements.
Maintain message access boundaries and brief templates.
Handle disputed reminders and actions lacking an accepted owner.
tasks.statement: Confer with project personnel to identify and resolve problems.

tasks.short: Discover customer needs and agree priorities for IT projects.

steps.what: Review existing customer requests and project history in the {PROJECT}.
Prepare interview questions and a survey draft in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Discovery brief and approved interview template.
loop.check: Manager checks relevance, neutral wording and unnecessary personal questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved questions return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but questions must reflect each customer's free-text concerns.

steps.what: Interview customers about problems, constraints and desired outcomes.
Issue surveys through the {WORKFLOW} and collect customer responses.
Combine customer notes and survey responses into a needs register in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Customer notes and survey responses with source identifiers.
loop.output: Draft needs register with themes, conflicting needs and source references.
loop.check: Manager checks source support, minority views and distinctions between requests and underlying needs.
loop.stop: Process one discovery batch with one correction pass; unresolved conflicts remain explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text descriptions express similar needs differently and sometimes conceal conflicting priorities.

steps.what: Validate needs and negotiate priorities with customer representatives.

tasks.design: A read-only integration gathers linked requests from the {PROJECT}, while configured forms in the {WORKFLOW} collect survey responses. Bounded drafting and classification loops prepare questions and a source-linked needs register in the {DOCS}; the manager approves survey sends and leads interviews and priority negotiations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests and interview notes sit in separate records. Templates help, but interpreting conflicting customer accounts still takes judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form configuration and modest integrations handle collection. Bounded text processing can prepare drafts, while coding assistance can reduce implementation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may disagree, omit constraints or describe preferred solutions rather than needs. Access restrictions can prevent combining their records.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice hesitation and negotiate whose needs take priority when resources are limited.

ambition.what: Include occasional users in discovery through accessible short surveys.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing conflicting needs with customers. They can recommend a broader evidence base; funding and scope authority remain delegated by the sponsor.

reach.task: Translate validated needs into testable requirements.
reach.learn: Requirement traceability, acceptance criteria and separating business needs from solution choices.

evidence.claim: Configured forms and record integrations can reduce collection and copying work; customer prioritisation still needs human judgement.
GitHub Copilot supports coding and review assistance with human oversight; this does not establish a particular build-speed improvement.

assumptions: The typical project combines customer interviews with occasional surveys; survey work is averaged across discovery cycles.
Customers may be internal business users or external customer representatives.
The conversation-heavy prior fits this task; the estimated mail share is lower because forms collect survey responses.
Build ranges describe an initial implementation using existing systems and permitted model processing, not a full research platform.
GDPR applies to identifiable responses. Employee consultation follows national rules where the survey design requires it.
unknowns: Whether customer requests have stable identifiers and permitted read access.
Which customer groups can be contacted and who approves survey distribution.
Whether sensitive information appears in discovery notes.
Which national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Does the source-linked needs register preserve conflicting and minority views?
Which groups respond poorly to surveys and need another discovery method?
new_work: Review drafted questions and grouped needs.
Resolve unsupported interpretations and conflicting responses.
Maintain survey templates, source links, permissions and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Assess current or future customer needs and priorities by communicating directly with customers, conducting surveys, or other methods.

tasks.short: Arrange and facilitate IT project meetings, then record decisions and actions.

steps.what: Review open issues in the {PROJECT} and decide whether a meeting is needed.
Chase attendee availability through the {EMAIL}.
Book a suitable time and send invitations through the {CALENDAR}.
Prepare an agenda and supporting material in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Meeting purpose, selected issues and pending decisions.
loop.output: Draft agenda with decisions required, owners and source links.
loop.check: Manager checks purpose, participants, sensitive content and time allocation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unclear objectives return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide the layout, but issue descriptions need synthesis into clear decision questions.

steps.what: Facilitate discussion, resolve disagreement and confirm decisions with participants.
Write minutes and an action list in the {DOCS}.

loop.output: Draft minutes and actions, with uncertain owners or dates marked.
loop.check: Manager verifies decisions, commitments and attribution against the notes.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; missing commitments stay unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes do not consistently distinguish discussion, proposals and agreed commitments.

steps.what: Publish minutes and assign agreed actions in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured availability rules in the {CALENDAR} replace routine scheduling exchanges through the {EMAIL}. Linked issues from the {PROJECT} feed bounded agenda and minutes drafting in the {DOCS}; the manager facilitates the meeting and approves publication of decisions and actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability chasing and action copying cross separate tools. Facilitation depends on trust and context that scheduling automation cannot supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared availability and configured action workflows cover the routine steps. Small text loops can turn selected issues and rough notes into reviewable drafts.
tasks.still_hard: External calendars, urgent conflicts and politically sensitive discussions need personal handling. Notes may not capture whether a commitment was actually agreed.
tasks.human_edge: Bring quiet participants into the discussion, challenge vague commitments and resolve conflict without damaging working relationships.

ambition.what: A cross-project blocker clinic for teams with unresolved dependencies.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing calendars and writing minutes, leaving more capacity for difficult discussions. They can choose asynchronous handling within their meeting remit; meeting automation grants no new project approval rights.

reach.task: Coordinate steering meetings around the decisions executives must make.
reach.learn: Decision-focused agendas, executive availability constraints and confidential distribution.

evidence.claim: Shared calendar configuration can replace routine internal availability chasing and booking.
Agenda and minutes drafting can use bounded text processing, but agreement and attribution need human checking.

assumptions: Routine internal meetings have shared free/busy access, agreed attendee lists and permitted booking windows.
External or exceptional bookings return to the manager rather than being booked automatically.
The initial design uses written notes and does not require recording or transcription.
The meeting-heavy prior fits this task; scheduling mail is a smaller, removable component.
Build ranges cover an internal pilot using existing calendar and project interfaces.
GDPR applies to notes and invitations. Recording or employee monitoring would require separate assessment and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Whether calendars expose sufficient free/busy information.
Which meetings include external participants or confidential material.
Who may approve action publication and amend disputed minutes.
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which recurring meetings can become asynchronous updates without delaying decisions?
How often do draft minutes mistake a proposal for an agreed action?
new_work: Review agendas, decision wording and action attribution.
Handle booking exceptions and disputed minutes.
Maintain booking rules, participant permissions and note retention.
tasks.statement: Schedule and facilitate meetings related to information technology projects.

tasks.short: Track milestones and deliverables, verify progress and surface exceptions.

steps.what: Inspect milestone dates, task completion and dependencies in the project record.
Ask delivery owners for missing dates, evidence and dependency updates.
Provide a progress update and links to deliverable evidence.
Reconcile owner updates and baseline dates in the tracking workbook.
Review weak evidence, conflicting updates and likely milestone slippage with delivery owners.
Publish milestone status and exception notes for project control.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} with milestone baselines, evidence links, owner update forms and stale-record reminders, removing the reconciliation workbook. A dashboard in the {PROJECT} shows date variance, blocked dependencies and evidence gaps, then publishes a standard status view after exceptions are resolved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates arrive as messages while baseline dates live elsewhere. Completion labels are often mistaken for evidence of an accepted deliverable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project fields, forms and dashboards can handle most tracking. Small deterministic extensions can check dependency dates and missing evidence without a model.
tasks.still_hard: An apparently complete task may conceal unfinished integration or acceptance work. Credible forecasts still depend on delivery owners reporting uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic progress claims and distinguish administrative completion from usable delivery.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly dependency resequencing for threatened milestones

tasks.altitude: The week centres on evidence gaps and blocked dependencies instead of collecting routine updates. The project manager can gain authority to resequence work within the approved baseline, with milestone changes still following change control.

reach.task: Analyse dependency paths and forecast milestone confidence.
reach.learn: Critical-path analysis, forecast calibration and acceptance evidence design.

evidence.claim: Structured milestone fields, baseline comparisons, reminders and dashboards can handle routine tracking without a model.
Removing workbook reconciliation requires owners to update the authoritative project record rather than a separate message chain.

assumptions: The baseline scenario includes a workbook bridging project records and owner messages; companies with integrated tracking may already avoid this work.
The future dashboard replaces the milestone comparison artefact, so no separate workbook is maintained.
Structured owner updates remain human; the design does not infer completion from message activity.
Shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates. Access and any consultation follow GDPR and national rules.
unknowns: Whether the {PROJECT} supports baselines, dependency checks and owner forms.
Which evidence is required before a deliverable counts as complete.
How often owners update records and how stale updates are handled.
Whether the proposed visibility changes trigger employee consultation.
research_questions: Which existing tracking fields can replace the workbook?
Do evidence-gap alerts identify slippage earlier than completion percentages?
What reminder frequency improves updates without creating noise?
new_work: Maintain milestone definitions, evidence requirements and dependency links.
Resolve stale updates and inconsistent completion claims.
Review alert usefulness and repair broken evidence links.
tasks.statement: Monitor or track project milestones and deliverables.

tasks.short: Negotiate project resources, supplier capacity and materials within agreed delivery and spending limits.

steps.what: Gather project requirements, capacity constraints and available budget.
Collect availability replies and supplier quotes against the resource brief.

loop.input: Selected availability replies and supplier quotes linked to the resource brief.
loop.output: Resource options with quantities, dates, prices, exclusions and source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields, currencies, units and arithmetic. The project manager checks ambiguous terms and missing replies.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reply formats vary, and qualifications often appear in free text. Use direct field mapping for structured quotes.

steps.what: Compare resource options, delivery effects and total costs.
Agree negotiation limits, priorities and acceptable trade-offs.
Negotiate timing, scope, price and resource commitments with stakeholders or suppliers.
Write agreed terms, unresolved points and approval requests.

loop.input: Negotiation notes, provisional agreement, supplier quotes and negotiation mandate.
loop.output: Agreement summary and approval request with source references and unresolved points.
loop.check: Compare prices, dates and quantities with source facts; flag mandate breaches and conflicting terms for review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; missing agreement evidence returns to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiated conditions and unresolved concessions appear in free-text notes. Templates handle layout but cannot reliably select these terms.

steps.what: Approve spending or resource allocation within delegated authority.
Record approved allocations or requisitions and update the project plan.

tasks.design: Configure a resource brief from {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}, then use bounded extraction on selected replies in {EMAIL} and deterministic calculations to produce an options comparison. Keep mandate setting and negotiation human; use a bounded drafting loop to prepare the agreement summary in {DOCS} and route approval through {WORKFLOW}. Approval triggers internal updates in {PROJECT} and requisition creation in {PROCUREMENT}, with duplicate checks and an exception queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity, budget and supplier terms sit in separate records and messages. Relationships and competing priorities also limit how much negotiation can follow fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and approval features can handle much of the structure. AI coding can help build missing adapters and calculations, while bounded extraction and drafting handle free text; the speed gain needs local measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can change before agreement. Supplier exclusions, competing project priorities and informal promises need human interpretation. Binding supplier acceptance remains subject to purchasing authority. GDPR applies to personal data, and EU AI Act obligations depend on the use; employee monitoring or allocation tools may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Read hesitation, build trust and trade timing against scope without damaging a working relationship. Decide when an apparently cheap offer creates unacceptable delivery dependence.

ambition.what: Weekly capacity-versus-supplier trade-off review for projects approaching a resource shortfall.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time assembling comparisons and recording agreements, leaving more time for negotiation and delivery choices. Spending and staffing decision rights remain with existing approvers.

reach.task: Compare internal capacity, supplier support and project resequencing.
reach.learn: Total-cost modelling, sensitivity analysis and the limits of estimated benefits.

reach.task: Translate a resource request into technical dependencies and acceptance conditions.
reach.learn: System dependencies, skill requirements and how scope changes affect delivery risk.

evidence.claim: Configured reports, deterministic comparisons and approval-triggered updates are feasible patterns; this exact negotiation workflow is not documented in the digest.
Negotiation depends on trust and contextual trade-offs, while its preparation and paperwork offer more scope for automation.
GitHub Copilot supports coding assistance and review, with oversight expected; this supports implementation assistance rather than a guaranteed build-time reduction.
Developer field trials reported more completed tasks with AI assistance; they do not establish a 10-to-100-fold speed gain for this workflow.
An early-2025 randomised developer study found slower completion with AI assistance, showing that implementation gains depend on context.
Staff evaluation or allocation based on personal characteristics can engage the EU AI Act employment provisions; scope depends on the actual use.

assumptions: The estimates cover one team, one comparison template and a small set of existing systems.
Approved reports or exports can provide project budgets, commitments and capacity without collecting new employee activity data.
The project manager negotiates within a mandate; commitments outside that mandate require approval.
The budget holder has authority for the commitment; additional signatories follow existing delegation rules.
Internal staffing cases skip supplier-specific fields and requisitions.
Step shares are modelling assumptions. They retain the supplied prior's emphasis on communication while making preparation and recording explicit.
Consultation and access estimates represent effort and routine waiting; national procedures can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which systems hold reliable capacity, budget and purchasing commitments.
Whether existing licences support the required reports, approvals and internal updates.
How much negotiation happens through meetings, messages or formal procurement rounds.
Who can reserve staff, approve spending and legally bind the organisation.
Whether supplier quotes can be processed in the approved model environment.
Which national consultation rules and existing employee agreements apply.
Whether any proposed use evaluates employees or allocates tasks based on personal characteristics.
Whether APIs, exports and service-account access are available.
research_questions: Can existing reporting and approval configuration remove the need for custom adapters?
How accurately does bounded extraction preserve exclusions, validity dates and conditional pricing across representative quotes?
Which comparison fields change negotiation decisions enough to justify maintaining them?
Does the pilot reduce preparation time without increasing agreement corrections or approval delays?
new_work: Review extracted qualifications, missing replies and conflicting agreement terms.
Maintain comparison formulas, approval thresholds and source-field mappings.
Resolve failed or duplicate internal updates.
Keep access, retention and model-processing settings current.
Sample agreement summaries against source notes and track corrections.
tasks.statement: Negotiate with project stakeholders or suppliers to obtain resources or materials.

tasks.short: Assess proposed project changes, obtain approval and update the delivery baseline.

steps.what: Read change requests arriving through the {EMAIL} and clarify missing details.

loop.input: Change request text and the change-record schema.
loop.output: Draft change record with missing fields marked.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; manager resolves ambiguous scope.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; incomplete requests enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: A structured form handles new requests, but email requests still require free-text extraction.

steps.what: Retrieve the current baseline and dependencies from the {PROJECT}.
Calculate schedule and cost scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Review feasibility, dependencies and delivery risks with technical leads.
Prepare a change recommendation in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Calculated scenarios, technical assessment and validated priorities.
loop.output: Draft recommendation showing options, assumptions and unresolved risks.
loop.check: Copy figures from calculated fields; manager checks reasoning and source support.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported recommendations return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: The calculation is deterministic, but explaining project-specific trade-offs requires narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Approve, reject or defer the change within delegated authority.
Update the baseline in the {PROJECT} and notify affected staff through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A change register in the {WORKFLOW} links requests to versioned baselines in the {PROJECT}, with deterministic schedule and cost scenarios on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Bounded loops extract email requests and draft recommendations in the {DOCS}; a delegated approver decides. Approved changes trigger checked baseline updates and notices through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change requests, estimates and approval records are scattered. Schedule arithmetic is straightforward, but feasibility and competing commitments are not.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records, dependency calculations and configured approvals already support much of the work. Coding assistance makes the missing connections easier to build.
tasks.still_hard: Effort estimates remain uncertain, resource dependencies may be incomplete and approved changes can conflict across projects.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a change is worth its disruption and negotiate credible commitments with delivery teams and sponsors.

ambition.what: Weekly scope-versus-date option decisions before the next steering meeting.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding change packs and more time comparing options with technical leads. Faster preparation supports decisions within existing approval limits; wider budget authority requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Compare change options against expected business benefits.
reach.learn: Sensitivity analysis, benefit assumptions and the cost of delaying a decision.

evidence.claim: Versioned change records, dependency calculations and approval workflows can automate preparation and controlled publication.
GitHub Copilot offers coding and review assistance that can support implementation, with oversight expected.
Developer field trials found productivity gains, but their results do not establish the build time for this workflow.

assumptions: The change approver is the manager within delegated limits and a sponsor or change board beyond them.
The {SPREADSHEET} currently joins estimates and rates that are not maintained together in the {PROJECT}.
Scenario calculations use human-supplied estimates; they do not predict effort automatically.
Publication checks approval scope and baseline version, and stops if either has changed.
Build ranges cover one project template and a limited set of integrations.
GDPR applies to identifiable project records; national consultation requirements depend on the implementation.
unknowns: Which changes the manager may approve.
Whether baseline versions, resource dependencies and cost rates are available through permitted interfaces.
Whether contractual customer approval is required for particular changes.
Which consultation and access approvals are required.
research_questions: Which scenario calculations can the existing {PROJECT} support through configuration?
How often do baseline conflicts or missing estimates prevent safe automatic publication?
new_work: Review extracted requests and drafted recommendations.

tasks.statement: Initiate, review, or approve modifications to project plans.

tasks.short: Define supplier needs, compare proposals, test suitability and secure selection approval.

steps.what: Write project needs, selection criteria and proposal requirements.
Approve sourcing scope, selection criteria and spending envelope.
Find eligible suppliers using approved supplier records and prior engagements.
Invite shortlisted suppliers to submit proposals.
Register received proposals and identify missing attachments.
Extract and compare scope, costs, exclusions and delivery evidence.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and the approved comparison fields.
loop.output: Evidence grid with source locations, exclusions and unknown fields; totals calculated deterministically.
loop.check: Require source locations, verify currencies and totals, and review material scope differences.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per proposal; unresolved fields remain unknown for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scope, exclusions and evidence appear in differently worded documents rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Test delivery claims through demonstrations, references and technical discussions.
Weight trade-offs and recommend a supplier with documented reasons.
Approve the supplier selection under delegated procurement authority.

tasks.design: Configure a sourcing record and approval flow in the {PROCUREMENT}, with proposal documents in the {DOCS} and controlled invitations through the {EMAIL}. A template generator prepares the brief, while a bounded extraction loop builds a source-linked evidence grid and deterministic code checks costs. People conduct demonstrations, recommend the supplier and approve selection before contracting starts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier records were available, but proposals differed in structure and wording. Suitability depended on delivery credibility and technical discussions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured sourcing records handle tracking and approvals. Bounded extraction can prepare a comparison without delegating the supplier decision.
tasks.still_hard: Omitted costs, weak references and ambiguous scope can survive document checks. Procurement thresholds, security requirements and contract terms vary.
tasks.human_edge: People challenge supplier claims, assess working relationships and accept the trade-offs between price, capability and delivery risk.

ambition.what: Departmental teams buying small IT consulting engagements.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into registering proposals and copying comparison fields. The project manager can support smaller buying teams; supplier approval rights remain with the authorised procurement role.

reach.task: Coordinate supplier onboarding after selection.
reach.learn: Learn required supplier checks, approval thresholds and the handoff from selection to contract.

evidence.claim: Sourcing records, invitation templates and approval workflows can reduce administrative work while retaining human selection.
SharePoint autofill columns supports prompt-based document metadata extraction and warns about incorrect results; this is not evidence of supplier-selection quality.

assumptions: The baseline uses approved supplier records plus document proposals and human assessments.
Time shares are estimates; judgement and supplier conversations remain substantial.
The procurement manager represents the authorised selection approver; local delegation may require another role.
Contract negotiation and purchase-order release are separate downstream actions.

tasks.short: Agree project audiences, channels and cadence, then deliver updates and handle stakeholder concerns.

steps.what: Discuss information needs and sensitivities with business and technical leads.
Record audiences, channels, cadence and escalation routes.
Approve the communication plan and sensitive-message approval routes.
Schedule meetings and routine milestone notifications.
Write tailored updates from current project evidence.

loop.input: Approved report, decision log, audience-specific disclosure rules and message template.
loop.output: Audience-specific drafts with source references and proposed recipient groups.
loop.check: Check facts against sources, enforce allowed fields and validate recipients against the approved plan.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per audience; fall back to an approved template with factual fields.
loop.why_not_simpler: Different audiences need different explanations of the same free-text decisions and risks.

steps.what: Approve update wording and check restricted recipients.
Send approved updates and authorised routine reminders.
Handle stakeholder concerns and agree follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Store audience groups, cadence and approval routes in the {PROJECT}, and configure scheduling through the {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW}. Approval binds the wording and recipients before the {EMAIL} or {CHAT} sends updates; sensitive messages follow the sponsor route.
tasks.previous_blocker: Communication plans were static documents, while recipients and project facts changed. Tailoring messages and handling concerns were mixed with scheduling and distribution.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured schedules and approval records handle routine coordination. A bounded drafting loop can reuse approved evidence for several audiences without generating new commitments.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may distrust accurate updates or need difficult conversations. Recipient changes, confidentiality and implied commitments require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager recognises concerns, chooses the right moment to communicate and negotiates understanding across technical and business groups.

ambition.what: Frontline operational teams affected by IT project changes.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into calendars, copying facts and distributing updates, leaving more time for affected teams. Communication approval remains delegated as before; sensitive commitments still need sponsor approval.

reach.task: Coordinate sponsor meetings and decision follow-ups.
reach.learn: Learn decision deadlines, confidentiality needs and how to turn meeting outcomes into tracked actions.

evidence.claim: Configured schedules, audience records and approval-bound notifications can reduce communication administration.
TOPdesk summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review; this supports the bounded drafting pattern, not proven project-communication gains.

Time shares are estimates; relationship work remains substantial.
Distribution uses the exact approved content and recipient list; changes invalidate approval.
Routine reminders use templates and audiences authorised in the communication plan.

tasks.short: Identify initial and additional project resource needs.

tasks.short: Build annual IT project budgets, agree funding priorities and monitor spending against forecasts.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts towards testing cost assumptions and discussing emerging funding choices. Forecast recommendations become more frequent; authority to approve spending stays unchanged.

reach.task: Compare project funding scenarios with expected operational benefits.
reach.learn: Learn benefit assumptions, sensitivity analysis and the difference between committed and avoidable costs.

evidence.claim: Structured cost reconciliation, scenario arithmetic and variance reporting can use deterministic technology.
GitHub Copilot supports assisted coding and review; the digest provides no documented case of this project-budget workflow.

Time shares are estimates; reducing preparation does not remove budget judgement.

steps.what: Gather approved objectives, requirements, architecture decisions, funding and resource decisions.

loop.output: Proposed work breakdown with source links and uncertain dependencies flagged.

loop.stop: One proposal and one correction pass; unresolved scope goes back to the project manager.

steps.what: Set durations, calendars, staffing and costs; reconcile schedule conflicts.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} as the plan record, with configured calendars, dependency checks, baselines and approved-change notifications. An integration links approved evidence from the {DOCS} and {ERP}, and a bounded loop proposes the work breakdown for review. Sponsor approval freezes a baseline; a versioned view replaces manual copying into a parallel document.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements, schedules and approval papers drift apart. Delivery templates help, but each project's scope still needs interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning features can handle schedules and baselines. AI coding makes the remaining adapters and evidence links easier to build, while a bounded loop assists decomposition.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies can be political or undiscovered. Technical estimates and owner commitments need challenge before a schedule becomes credible.
tasks.human_edge: Turn ambiguous goals into shared commitments and negotiate scope when time, funding and quality conflict.

tasks.design: A reusable importer gathers approved material from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}; a bounded drafting loop proposes work packages with source references and open questions. Configured hierarchy checks and baseline controls in {PROJECT} support technical review and sponsor approval, while shared views replace the parallel {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements varied, project templates were inconsistent, and transferring agreed detail into the plan took effort.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building importers and validators. Bounded drafting can propose an initial decomposition, with no assumed breakthrough in estimation.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden dependencies, architecture choices and incomplete scope still require technical discussion. Connectors and custom project fields can dominate implementation effort.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising omitted work and deciding which boundaries make delivery manageable.
